sources.locator: React Learn and Reference; React 19.2; provisions applicable to React developer tools
sources.claim: React DevTools inspect component trees, props, state, context, and profiling for a particular development render.

canonicalExplanation.summary: The React DevTools browser extension adds two panels. **Components** shows the component tree with each one's current **props, state and context**, so you can see where a wrong value first appears. **Profiler** records an interaction and shows which components rendered, **why**, and **how long** each took. A highlighted re-render isn't automatically a problem: re-rendering is how React works. Only optimise when the profiler shows something is actually **slow**, then measure again to prove the fix helped.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
Typing in a lesson search box feels laggy. A teammate turns on "highlight updates", sees the whole page flash, and wants to wrap every component in memo. You open the Profiler first. A profiler shows an expensive list rerender before memoization is considered and measured again. In this lesson you'll locate and explain a component data-flow defect using developer-tool evidence.

```predict
{"question": "\"Highlight updates\" shows 20 components flashing on each keypress. What should you do first?", "options": ["Wrap all 20 in memo", "Record in the Profiler to see which renders actually take time"], "answer": 1, "why": "Most re-renders are cheap. Measure to find the one that's slow."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Modular browser application**, **Declarative UI and re-rendering** (why components run again), and **Sources, console and debugger** (the browser's own panels).

sections.heading: The model: inspect data, then measure time
sections.body:
| Question | Panel | What to look at |
|---|---|---|
| Why is this value wrong? | Components. | select the component; read props and state, then its parent's. |
| Where does the value come from? | Components. | walk up the tree until the value is first wrong. |
| Why did it re-render? | Profiler, with "record why" on. | "props changed: items" or "parent rendered". |
| Is it slow? | Profiler flame chart. | render duration in milliseconds per component. |

```text
Profiler recording: typed "arr" (3 commits).
  SearchPage     0.4 ms   why: state changed (query)
  SearchBox      0.2 ms   why: props changed (value)
  LessonList    38.0 ms   why: parent rendered      <- the slow one.
    LessonRow x 900  (each ~0.04 ms)
```

```reveal
{"prompt": "What does \"why: parent rendered\" tell you?", "answer": "LessonList's own props didn't change; it re-rendered only because SearchPage did. That's the case memo can skip, if it's worth it."}
```

sections.heading: Find a data-flow defect

includes: Inspect props, state and context in the Components panel to trace data flow.
Record and read a Profiler session before and after an optimisation.

outcomes: Locate and explain a component data-flow defect using developer-tool evidence.

examples.title: Measuring before memoizing
examples.situation: A profiler shows an expensive list rerender before memoization is considered and measured again.
walkthrough: **Record:** typing "arr" in the Profiler shows LessonList taking 38 ms per keypress, marked "parent rendered".
**Consider memoization:** wrapping LessonList in memo, with a stable lessons array, lets React skip it when only the query changes.
**Measure again:** a second recording will show LessonList skipped and each commit under 2 ms.
examples.result: Typing feels instant, and the change is backed by before-and-after profiler evidence rather than guesswork.

examples.title: The avatar that showed the wrong person
examples.situation: On a class page, each student's card shows the teacher's avatar.
walkthrough: In Components, StudentCard's avatarUrl prop holds the teacher's URL.
Its parent, ClassList, passes `avatarUrl={teacher.avatar}` by mistake.
Fix the prop in ClassList to `student.avatar` and confirm the prop in DevTools.
examples.result: Every card shows the right student's avatar, and the fix was found by following props up the tree.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Every highlighted rerender must be removed with memoization.
misconceptions.correction: Re-rendering is normal and usually cheap. Memoization adds complexity and only helps when a render is measurably slow; use the Profiler to find that render and to confirm the fix.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Measuring before memoizing", which component was actually slow?

analogy.example: DevTools is like a **mechanic's diagnostic tool**. The Components panel reads each part's current values (props and state). The Profiler is the **stopwatch on each part** while the engine runs. You don't replace every part that moves; you replace the one that's slow.
limitations: Cars have one engine; apps have many components rendering in commits.
Always test-drive again after the repair: measure twice.

steps.explanation: The profiler shows an expensive list rerender while typing.
The list re-renders only because its parent did, so memoization is considered.
A second recording confirms the change helped.

trace.textAlternative: Profiling a slow list. Step 1, Record: commits is 3; LessonList is 38 ms each. The profiler shows an expensive list rerender while typing. Step 2, Diagnose: why is parent rendered; props changed is none. The list re-renders only because its parent did, so memoization is considered. Step 3, Measure again: LessonList is skipped; commit is < 2 ms. A second recording confirms the change helped.

faded.prompt: For "Measuring before memoizing", explain how a profiler shows an expensive list rerender before memoization is considered and measured again.
expectedEvidence: Names the example "Measuring before memoizing": the profiler shows an expensive list rerender.
Memoization is considered only after measuring.
Typing feels instant, backed by before-and-after evidence.

nearTransfer.prompt: A cart total shows 0 even though items are listed. Describe how you'd use the Components panel to find which component first has the wrong value.
scaffold: Walk up to where items are stored.
expectedEvidence: Find the first component with a wrong value.
Name the prop or state to fix.

farTransfer.prompt: Profile one interaction in your React app. Record it, identify the slowest component and why it rendered, try one fix, and write a before/after note with the numbers.
scaffold: Turn on "record why each component rendered".
Change one thing at a time.
expectedEvidence: A clear explanation of the cause.

remediation.explanation: For wrong values: **walk up the Components tree to the first wrong prop or state.** For slowness: **record, find the biggest bar, read why, change one thing, record again.**
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The avatar that showed the wrong person".

recap.summary: To locate and explain a component defect using developer-tool evidence, use the Components panel to follow props, state and context up the tree to where a value first goes wrong, and use the Profiler to find which render is actually slow and why, optimising only with before-and-after measurements.
retrievalPrompts: Which panel shows props and state?
